dateline: Hawthorne, CA / Boca Chica, TX — May 2002–Present
heroHeadline: FAA Grounds Starship After IFT-12 Anomaly — 6th Grounding; IFT-13 Delayed to July–August 2026; IPO Roadshow 7 Days Away (June 4)
heroSubtitle: 8,787 days since SpaceX founding — The FAA formally grounded Starship following the IFT-12 Booster 19 boostback anomaly (May 22), requiring a mishap investigation before IFT-13 can receive a new launch license. IFT-13 (Booster 20 + Ship 40) now targets July–August 2026; SpaceX may revert to a Gulf splashdown profile for the booster rather than a Mechazilla catch. The Starship grounding is being covered as a material risk factor for the SpaceX Nasdaq (SPCX) IPO, with the management roadshow 7 days away (June 4–11), pricing June 11, and debut June 12 targeting a $75–80B raise at $1.75–2T implied valuation. SpaceX has completed 65 orbital missions in 2026 and 616 cumulative booster recoveries; Starlink constellation: 10,480+ active satellites, 10.3M subscribers.
